Char: Study name: Comparison between switching from intravenous to subcutaneous infliximab on the maintenance of clinical and biochemical remission in patients with inflammatory bowel disease
Char: Interventions:
Intervention - switching patients from intravenous infliximab to subcutaneous infliximab for the treatment of inflammatory bowel disease

Control - continuing intravenous infliximab for the treatment of inflammatory bowel disease
Char: Outcomes:
Primary

  • Composite primary outcome: Comparing the proportion of patients who remain in clinical remission

Secondary

  • Comparing the change in infliximab trough level in the IV infliximab group versus the SC infliximab group using a blood sample
  • Patient satisfaction in the SC infliximab group using a survey with a 5-point Likert scale
  • Comparing the change in faecal calprotectin in the IV infliximab group versus the SC infliximab group using stool samples
  • Comparing the change in medical therapy between the IV infliximab and SC infliximab group (using data-linkage to medical records): Need for corticosteroids
  • Comparing other standard of care biochemical monitoring of patients on infliximab using a blood sample
  • Pharmacovigilance of potential treatment-associated adverse effects, assessed in accordance with the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events
  • Comparing the change in medical therapy between the IV infliximab and SC infliximab group (using data linkage to medical records): Adding immunomodulator
  • Comparing the change in medical therapy between the IV infliximab and SC infliximab group (using data-linkage to medical records): Need for dose-escalation
  • Comparing the change in medical therapy between the IV infliximab and SC infliximab group (using data-linkage to medical records): Switching to another biological agent
  • Comparing the change in medical therapy between the IV infliximab and SC infliximab group (using data-linkage to medical records): Need for IBD surgery
  • Comparing the change in infliximab antibodies in the IV infliximab group versus the SC infliximab group using a blood sample
Char: Notes:
Retrospectively registered. Anticipated end date: 1 October 2023

Sponsor: Celltrion

Char: Outcomes:
Primary: 

Rate of disease relapse

Secondary:

Change in serum infliximab drug levels in each group measured on 12-weekly blood tests

Rates of clinical relapse in each group, defined as: modified HBI >/=5 in CD patients, partial Mayo Score >/=2 in UC patients measured on clinical surveys.

Rates of biochemical disease relapse in each group, defined as: CRP >5 mg/L, or FCP >250 µg/g post-first dose of either IV or SC infliximab within the study. CRP and FCP measured on 12-weekly blood and faecal tests.

Rate of dose-intensification due to clinical and biochemical relapse in each group post-first dose of either IV or SC infliximab within the study collected on a study-specific database.

Change in faecal calprotectin in each group measure on 12-weekly faecal tests.

Change in CRP in each group measured on 12-weekly blood tests.

Antibodies to infliximab in each group measured on 12-weekly blood tests.

Adverse events in each group (including infusion or injection site reaction, hypersensitivity, rash, lymphopenia, infection) using a study-specific questionnaire 12-weekly.

Patient satisfaction (Likert scale satisfaction survey) questionnaire.

Rate of refusal to switch from IV to subcutaneous infliximab and proportion of patients switched to subcutaneous who elect to switch back to IV recorded on a study-specific database.

Cost differences for:
Healthcare service - infusion centre (mean chair time, nursing staff costs), drug costs (product, pharmacy preparation)
Patients - workdays lost, transport and parking
Collected by review of hospital financial records at select sites.
 

Composite adherence (number of missed doses, number of rescheduled doses) and any impact of COVID-19 on adherence (yes/no). Collected on 12-weekly surveys designed specifically for this study. 

Success of further dose-intensification in each group as measured by an increment in drug levels and rate of recapture of clinical and biochemical response (defined as achieving the same remission parameters required to qualify for study enrolment) collected on 12-weekly blood tests, faecal tests and either the partial Mayo score or HBI, as appropriate.

Health-related quality of life (Inflammatory Bowel Disease Questionnaire - IBD-Q)

Char: Study name: Anti-tumour necrosis factor discontinuation in inflammatory bowel disease patients in remission: study protocol of a prospective, multicentre, randomized clinical trial
Char: Interventions:
Intervention- patients in group 1 continue their current antiTNF treatment (infliximab or adalimumab)

Control: Patients in group 2 are given a placebo matched to the drug they were previously receiving.
Char: Outcomes:
Primary outcome: The primary objective of this study is to compare the rates of clinical remission at 1 year in patients who discontinue treatment with an anti-TNF agent versus those who continue.

Secondary outcome: the duration of relapse-free time; mucosal healing; quality of life (QoL) and work productivity; safety; and the identification of predictive factors for relapse.
Char: Notes:
The published abstract does not separate between CD and UC patients

Funding: The Instituto de Salud Carlos III (PI15/00560). Project financed with FEDER funds.

Char: Study name: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of ABBV-154 in Subjects with Moderately to Severely Active Crohn's Disease (CD): AIM-CD
Char: Outcomes:
Primary end point(s): The primary endpoint is the achievement of endoscopic response at Week 12 in the Induction Period defined as a decrease in Simple Endoscopic Score for Crohn’s Disease (SES-CD17) > 50% from Baseline (or for subjects with isolated ileal disease and a Baseline SES-CD of 4, at least a 2-point reduction from Baseline). 

Secondary Objective: The secondary objectives are to assess the pharmacokinetics (PK), pharmacodynamics (PD), and immunogenicity of ABBV 154.
